newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Britons to require visas to stay in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Britons to require visas to stay in Hong Kong.

text.p: British citizens who want to work, study or settle in Hong Kong will need visas from April 1, the territory's government said on Thursday.

The government said it will implement administrative changes to bring the immigration status of British citizens in line with that of other foreign nationals as the British territory nears its handover to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
British citizens will be able to visit Hong Kong visa-free for up to six months under the new rules, the statement said.
If they want to work, study or settle in Hong Kong, they will have to obtain a visa in the same way as other foreign nationals, and the same criteria for approval will apply, it said.
Previously, Britons could visit, work or study in Hong Kong for up to one year without restriction.
Those already with firm plans to come to Hong Kong to work, study or settle will be able to apply for a change of status during their six-month period as visitors.
British citizens who have resided in Hong Kong for seven years and acquired the right to land can continue to enter and remain in Hong Kong without any restrictions, it said.
Those who have been in the territory for less than seven years will be allowed to stay until their limit of stay expires.

The statement quoted an Immigration Department spokesman as saying it was the government's intention to remove other rights enjoyed exclusively by British citizens. This would be a separate exercise requiring legislation, it said.
"These include the right to land and the special deportation and removal arrangements. The proposed changes will be implemented as soon as the bill is enacted," the spokesman said.
Legislation eliminating special rights for British citizens remains stalled in the legislature.

Under current rules, Britons receive a new one-year visa stamp every time they enter the territory. Macau, an hour's ferry ride from the territory, is a favourite destination for those seeking visa renewals.
Representatives of tourism-related businesses in Macau said on Thursday they had not seen any marked surge in Britons travelling to the Portuguese-run enclave.
"We have not noticed any increase in the number of British nationals travelling to Macau, but we are prepared for it," Macau Ferry Terminal manager Augusto Lizardo said.
